description: Handwritten Lean source declarations, their nonexclusive mathematical-node memberships, and witnessed source-module dependencies.

node_associations.interpretation: These are transitive declaration reachability associations. Edges require a referenced prerequisite declaration outside the consumer node's own registered declarations; shared-root membership is listed separately. A multiply associated declaration is not an independently owned mathematical prerequisite. This graph is not asserted to be a DAG.

declaration_membership_policy.declarations: Only handwritten Lean declarations are public source vertices. Structure and class declarations include their written fields and constructor requirements.
declaration_membership_policy.nodes: A handwritten declaration may contribute to several mathematical nodes. These registered memberships are nonexclusive associations.
declaration_membership_policy.sources: Each source entry identifies a handwritten .lean file, module and declaration line. The catalog includes standalone declarations without adding them as mathematical-node roots.
declaration_membership_policy.dependencies: Source dependencies retain type, proof or definition-body, and structure-field prerequisites. Internal elaboration details are contracted to handwritten endpoints, including dependency paths through library proofs.
declaration_membership_policy.library_reuse: Library reuse identifies handwritten source modules and explicitly located source interfaces. It does not catalog compiled files or internal compiler declarations.
declaration_membership_policy.edge_direction: Edges point from a prerequisite handwritten source declaration to its consumer. Module edges summarize these source dependencies and do not arise merely from imports.

AtiyahSinger.ComplexBundle.ContinuousHer.definition_scope: Positive definite Hermitian fiber forms with continuous pairing in the original total-space topology, together with finite-rank local triviality of that same complex bundle. Rank may vary between components and may be zero.

written_fields.name: isFiniteRank
written_fields.description: Actual locally finite-rank local triviality in the same original total-space topology.

AtiyahSinger.HasSymbolExpansion.definition_scope: The remainder estimates for a specified formal symbol sequence and specified orders. Strict decrease of those orders and convergence to negative infinity are supplied separately by clients when the full classical asymptotic-expansion convention is required.

AtiyahSinger.IsSmoothHermitianBundle.definition_scope: The original complex vector bundle has real-smooth transitions and its fixed fiber inner product has real-smooth Gram coefficients in its specified atlas. This condition is defined over a charted base; smooth-manifold applications supply IsManifold separately.

parent_requirements.description: The parent condition supplies real-smooth transitions for that same original complex bundle.

AtiyahSinger.SmoothCliffordModule.definition_scope: The original smooth complex vector bundle carries a fiberwise Clifford action with real-smooth local coefficients in its specified atlas. Compatible Hermitian metric and connection data belong to the stronger Dirac-bundle structure.

references.locator: II.5, Clifford modules and Dirac bundles

written_fields.name: isSmoothBundle
written_fields.description: Real-smoothness of the same original complex bundle and its specified atlas.

AtiyahSinger.SmoothHermitianMetric.definition_scope: Positive definite Hermitian forms on the original complex vector bundle, with real-smooth Gram coefficients and real-smooth transition maps for that same atlas. This carrier is defined over a charted base; smooth-manifold applications supply IsManifold separately.

written_fields.name: isSmoothBundle
written_fields.description: Real-smooth transitions of the same original complex bundle atlas.

AtiyahSinger.fourierSG.definition_scope: The unnormalized angular-frequency Fourier transform with forward phase exp(-i x·ξ). Quantization uses the positive inverse phase exp(i x·ξ) and paired factor (2π)^(-n). SG III.2 uses a unitary normalization; its paired operator agrees with this convention.
